source_text: μεῖς εἰς πονηρίαν, καὶ ἀσυμφανῆ τοῖς πολλοῖς ἔν γε δὴ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς τὴν τῶν ἠθῶν ἔχοντες μοχθηρίαν. Παραπέφυκε δὲ ἀεὶ τοῖς τὴν ἐπάρατον ἀλαζονείαν ἠῤῥωστηκόσι, τὸ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐθέλειν οὓς ἂν δύναιντο τυχὸν, καὶ πολυτρόποις κακουργίας ἐκπολιορκεῖν εὑρήμασιν, καθαρπάζειν δὲ οὕτω, καὶ τοῦτο ἀπλήστως. Ταύτῃτοι συνάπτει λέγων εὐθύ· «Καὶ στρουθὸν καὶ λάρον.» Ἀπληστότατα γὰρ οἶμαι ταυτὶ, καὶ τὸ παρεμπίπτον ἀεὶ συλλέγοντα. Εἶτά φησιν, ὅτι «Καὶ ἱέρακα καὶ τὰ ὅμοια αὐτῷ, καὶ νυκτικόρακα, καὶ καταῤῥάκτην, καὶ ἴβιν, καὶ πορφυρί
pass_a_gloss: §24 dual gloss: ἁλιαίετος / sea-eagle · νυκτικόραξ / night-raven · φιλαλληλία / mutual-love … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Proud/greedy/night birds type violent and dark workers.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ...we unto wickedness, and having in themselves the wickedness of customs unclear for the many. And there has always grown-beside for those sick with cursed arrogance the wishing to greed those they can, and to besiege with many-mannered findings of evil-working, and thus to snatch-away, and this greedily. In this way he joins saying straight: 'And sparrow and gull.' For most greedy I think these, always collecting what falls in. Then: 'And hawk and the like, and night-raven, and diver, and ibis, and purple-gallinule, and pelican, and swan.' These write-down upon themselves those plotting harshly against others and springing-upon unrestrainedly whom they can, so as not to refuse even danger upon life. For the hawk leaps-down upon every weaker winged one; diver, ibis, purple-gallinule, pelican rage-upon fishes and make food their destruction. Such are all, as far as manners and wildness, who reckon as nothing destroying some for what is pleasant to themselves; who having thrust-aside mutual-love and struck-against love's ordinances would hear: 'Do not seek the of yourselves, but also the of others; for love does not work evil for the neighbor.' And needing to refuse he said again owl, heron, plover and the like, hoopoe and bat. These are night-loving, rejoicing in the dark, practicing flight as sweetest in it, hating sun's light and not bearing to act in it; and such clearly are workers of the worthless. For true is what Christ said, that 'Everyone doing worthless things'
